prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The five views show an indoor counter area, with shelving and a chair to the left, a counter and tall refrigerator/display near the centre, and a glass-fronted case to the right; brighter tones separate nearby counter edges, hands, and equipment from darker walls and background openings. The woman remains in front of the wearer across the sequence, approximately 1.5–3 m away at first and about 0.7–1.2 m away in the final frames, while the wearer’s hands and the red basket are within roughly 0.2–0.7 m; nearby counter objects are generally within about 0.5–1.5 m of her. The changing brightness and apparent scale support a rightward turn and approach toward the woman and counter, while left-side shelving and the chair move out of view and the right display becomes more prominent. Depth makes near/far layering and occlusion boundaries clearer than RGB, including hands and counter items partly blocking one another, but distances are only rough because large regions have similar tones, object edges bleed, and reflective glass, dark openings, and cropped foreground objects appear unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The masks identify a chair on the far left, a person behind or beside the counter, a laptop, book and cup on the counter, a tall refrigerator near the centre, and later a television/display, chair, person and hairbrush-like object on the right. Early on, the labelled chair and shelving are several metres left of the wearer, the woman is roughly 1.5–3 m ahead, and the refrigerator is about 1–2 m behind or to her right; by the last frame she is around 0.7–1.2 m ahead-left, with the display and counter objects to her right and the wearer’s foreground items within arm’s reach. Her mask shifts from centre-right toward the right and grows, then appears nearer centre-left as the camera turns right and approaches; other small person masks are fragmented or likely duplicate detections rather than clearly separate people. Segmentation reveals object identities and overlap more explicitly than RGB, but it misses most shelves, counter structure, hands, and basket, confuses or inconsistently labels large fixtures as TV/refrigerator, and produces partial masks where objects are cropped or occluded.
descriptions.pose: The yellow body skeleton consistently places the woman ahead of the wearer, generally upright behind or beside the counter, with her upper body oriented increasingly toward the camera as the wearer approaches and turns right; facial keypoints suggest she looks roughly toward the wearer, although head direction is uncertain in several frames. Her arm extends laterally toward the counter in the second frame and bends nearer her torso in later frames, while the magenta hand detections appear low and close to the camera in frames three and five, roughly 0.2–0.7 m away and within the wearer’s arm reach. The woman is initially about 1.5–3 m away and not within the wearer’s reach, becoming roughly 0.7–1.2 m away in the final view; her own hands remain within her arm’s reach of the counter and nearby objects. Pose makes limb configuration, facing direction, and isolated hand locations clearer than RGB, but the skeleton is incomplete, distorted, or disconnected in every frame, the final horizontal limb segment is implausibly simplified, and some magenta points may merge hands with nearby foreground clutter or occlusion.
